Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak vrch, *verch, from Proto-Slavic *vьrxъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈvɛrx]
  • Rhymes: -ɛrx
  • Hyphenation: верх

Noun

[edit]

верх (verx) m inan (diminutive верщок, relational adjective верхнї)

  1. top, peak, summit (uppermost part of something)
    Antonym: дно (dno)
    верх древа ― verx dreva ― the top of a tree
    верх брега ― verx breha ― the peak of the hill
    верх бока ― verx boka ― top of the page
    од верха до дно ― od verxa do dno ― from top to bottom
  2. tip, extremity
    верх игли ― verx ihli ― tip of the needle
  3. lid, cover, brim (of pots etc.)
  4. pillow case, cover, wrapper
    Near-synonyms: заглавчина (zahlavčina), заглавок (zahlavok), покривка (pokrivka)
  5. surface
    Synonym: поверхносц (poverxnosc)
    риба плїва под самим верхом
    riba pljiva pod samim verxom
    the fish swims just below the surface
    муряч виплївал на верх
    murjač vipljival na verx
    the grebe emerged to the surface
  6. roof (of a building)
    Synonym: закрице (zakrice)
  7. flap (in a pocket)
    Synonym: патна (patna)
  8. front, façade (of clothes)
  9. (figuratively) top, climax, height, pinnacle, zenith
    Synonyms: венєц (venjec), вершина (veršina)
  10. (graph theory) vertex

Russian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vьrxъ (whence also Old Church Slavonic врьхъ (vrĭxŭ)), from Proto-Indo-European *wers-.

Balto-Slavic cognates include Lithuanian viršus and Latvian virsus. Other Indo-European cognates include Latin verruca (“a steep place, height”), Ancient Greek ἕρμα (hérma, “reef, rock, hill”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [vʲerx]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Noun

[edit]

верх • (verx) m inan (genitive ве́рха, nominative plural верхи́, genitive plural верхо́в)

  1. top, upper part, roof, dome, height
    • 1925, Михаил Булгаков [Mikhail Bulgakov], “Глава 8. История в совхозе”, in Роковые яйца; English translation from K. M. Cook-Horujy, transl., The Fateful Eggs, Moscow: Raduga Publishers, 1990:
      Зате́м верх бревна́ надломи́лся, немно́го склони́лся и над Алекса́ндром Семё́новичем оказа́лось что́-то напомина́ющее по высоте́ электри́ческий моско́вский столб.
      Zatém verx brevná nadlomílsja, nemnógo sklonílsja i nad Aleksándrom Semjónovičem okazálosʹ štó-to napominájuščeje po vysoté elektríčeskij moskóvskij stolb.
      Then the top of the log cracked, bent down slightly, and something about the height of a Moscow electric lamp-post loomed over Alexander Semyonovich.
  2. (figuratively) summit, apex
    совеща́ние в верха́х ― soveščánije v verxáx ― summit meeting
  3. the highest degree of something
    Э́то верх глу́пости! ― Éto verx glúposti! ― This is the height of stupidity!
  4. upper class
    Antonym: низ (niz)
  5. (arm-wrestling) top-roll
    Coordinate terms: крюк (krjuk), бок (bok), три́цепс (tríceps)

Noun

[edit]

верх • (verx) m inan (genitive ве́рха, nominative plural верха́, genitive plural верхо́в)

  1. right side (of clothing, fabric), shoe upper, boot top
  2. hood, top, soft top, rag top of a carriage or convertible automobile
  3. cap, cover, outside, shell (clothing, as opposed to a lining)

Ukrainian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vьrxъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ʋɛrx]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

верх • (verx) m inan (genitive ве́рху, nominative plural верхи́, genitive plural верхі́в)

  1. top, upper part
    Antonym: низ (nyz)
  2. surface
  3. (figurative) upper hand
  4. (colloquial, plural only) elite, leaders
  5. high notes, upper register
    Antonym: низи́ (nyzý)
